newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended lower for the third successive day as financial market attention was fixed on the Federal Reserve Open Market Committee's (FOMC) meeting.
Dealers said the quiet first day of trading after the Whit Monday holiday reflected uncertainty about the direction of U.S. interest rates, with an announcement due about 1815 GMT.
"People are waiting for the FOMC meeting," said a dealer.
Opinion is divided on the likely outcome, although those tipping a U.S. rate hike favour a 25 basis point increase.
Otherwise, the focus of domestic attention remained the narrowing yield spread between Dutch state loans and Bunds.
The Dutch yield discount to Germany ended at six basis points for 10-year paper, compared with 24 basis points at the start of the year and five last Friday.

Among the factors cited for the divergence are the Dutch inflation premium over Germany, the spate of recent guilder Eurobond issues and the expectation that sales of the 5.75 percent February 2007 bond will be reopened next Monday.
The Dutch Finance Ministry's agency will announce a new bond issue on Friday and it is widely tipped to be this bond, the 10-year benchmark in guilders.
A Reuter poll of economists last Friday found that the average expectation for the 10-year spread in one month's time was seven basis points below Germany.

Rabobank International said in a weekly note issued today that although it preferred Bunds at the long end of the yield curve, Dutch paper would represent a short term buy if German and Dutch yields converged.
It also said Dutch paper in the 1999 area was far more attractive, yielding 15 basis points over equivalent German paper.
